'''Kenneth D. Karlin''' (born October 30, 1948) is an American chemist and a professor of chemistry at [[Johns Hopkins University]] in Baltimore, Maryland.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://chemistry.jhu.edu/|title=Home {{!}} Department of Chemistry|work=Department of Chemistry|access-date=2018-05-24|language=en}}</ref>  He was born on October 30, 1948, in [[Pasadena, California]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://krieger.jhu.edu/chem/wp-content/uploads/sites/72/2016/05/KARLIN-Kenneth-D.-Full-CV-End-of-2015.pdf|title=Karlin CV}}</ref> Research in his group focuses on coordination chemistry relevant to biological and environmental processes, involving copper or [[heme]] complexes.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://sites.krieger.jhu.edu/karlin/|title=Home {{!}} Kenneth D. Karlin Research Group|work=Kenneth D. Karlin Research Group|access-date=2018-05-24|language=en}}</ref> Of particular interest are reactivities of such complexes with nitrogen oxides, O<sub>2</sub>, and the oxidation of substrates by the resultant compounds. He is also the Editor-in-Chief of the book series ''Progress in Inorganic Chemistry''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/series/2229|title=Progress in Inorganic Chemistry |website=onlinelibrary.wiley.com|language=en|access-date=2018-05-24}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* Maryland Chemist of the Year Award (American Chemical Society Maryland Section), 2011<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://maryland.sites.acs.org/marylandchemistaward.htm|title=Maryland Chemist Award|website=Maryland Section|access-date=2018-05-24|archive-date=2014-02-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140224215357/http://maryland.sites.acs.org/marylandchemistaward.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* F. Albert Cotton Award in Synthetic Inorganic Chemistry, 2009<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/f-albert-cotton-award-in-synthetic-inorganic-chemistry.html|title=F. Albert Cotton Award in Synthetic Inorganic Chemistry – American Chemical Society|website=American Chemical Society|language=en|access-date=2018-05-24}}</ref>
* 2009 Sierra Nevada Distinguished Chemist Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chem.unr.edu/acs/|title=Sierra Nevada Local Section, American Chemical Society|website=www.chem.unr.edu|access-date=2018-05-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190126164347/http://www.chem.unr.edu/acs/|archive-date=2019-01-26|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Appointed to [[Ira Remsen]] Chair in Chemistry, Johns Hopkins University, May 1999.
* Elected Chair, 1998 Metals in Biology Gordon Research Conference
* "MERIT" Award, 1993–2003, National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIH)
* Fellow, American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) – elected October, 1992
* 1991 Buck-Whitney Award (ACS Eastern New York Section Research Award)
* University "Excellence in Research" Award, [[SUNY at Albany]], 1988
* General Electric Visiting Faculty Research Fellow, GE R&D Center, Schenectady, NY, 1986–87

== Positions ==
* 1977–1983	          Assistant Professor: Department of Chemistry, SUNY at Albany, Albany, NY
* 1983–1987	          Associate Professor: Department of Chemistry, SUNY at Albany, Albany, NY
* 1987–1990	          Professor: Department of Chemistry, SUNY at Albany, Albany, NY
* 1990–present	  Professor: Department of Chemistry, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD
* 2009–present Professor: Department of Bioinspired Science, WCU Program, MOBIC (Metal Oxygen BioInspired Chemistry) Group [[Ewha Womans University]] Seoul, KOREA

== Personal ==
Karlin is the son of Stanford mathematician [[Samuel Karlin]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/02/21/us/21karlin.html|title=Samuel Karlin, Versatile Mathematician, Dies at 83|first=Douglas|last=Martin|work=The New York Times |date=February 21, 2008|via=NYTimes.com}}</ref>
